column1: Damage{{efn|All damage totals are in 2015 [[United States dollars|USD]] unless otherwise stated.|group=note|name=Damage}}

column2: A couple of hardwood trees were split and large tree limbs were downed.
column3: A sheet metal roof was blown across the street at a farmstead. Several trees were snapped in a cemetery.
column5: A tornado was broadcast on live television via news helicopter.
column6: An off-duty National Weather Service employee reported a tornado.
column7: At least four homes sustained damage to their roofs, windows, or siding, including one that had a large section of its roof removed. A garage was destroyed, with inside vehicles moved {{convert|30|–|50|ft|m|abbr=on}}. Other outbuildings, trees, power poles, and trees were damaged or destroyed.
column8: Several homes and outbuildings sustained damage, of which two houses sustained considerable damage. One of those two homes was unanchored and slid off of its foundation, while the second lost its entire roof structure. A large metal building with wood post frame construction was destroyed. Widespread tree damage was observed, irrigation pivots were damaged, and a train car was derailed as well.
column9: A large multiple-vortex wedge tornado caused significant damage to numerous homes and other structures in Bridge Creek. Trees and power poles were snapped, mobile homes were completely destroyed, and frame homes were heavily damaged, a few of which lost roofs and exterior walls. One poorly-anchored frame home was leveled, and vehicles from some residences were tossed over 100 yards away. A total of 1,500 homes and mobile home were damaged by the tornado, including 200 that were severely damaged or destroyed. Outbuildings were destroyed as well.
column10: Trained storm spotters reported a brief tornado.
column11: Pivots were overturned, power poles were snapped, and trees were damaged. A home sustained damage to its porch.
column12: Numerous pivots were overturned, power poles were snapped, and widespread tree damage occurred. A few buildings sustained minor damage. Several outbuildings and grain bins were damaged or destroyed, and a few homes lost portions of their roofs in rural areas as well.
column13: A storm chaser observed a satellite tornado in conjunction with the previous EF3 tornado east of Amber.
column14: Three center pivot irrigation systems were damaged. At one farmstead, a single car detached garage was damaged and a carport was ripped from a barn. At a second farmstead, one home unsecured from its foundation was completely leveled, another home sustained significant damage, and a barn was rendered a complete loss. A small hog barn had its roof ripped off. Numerous trees were snapped or debarked.
column15: A home sustained roof, window, and siding damage, tree and power line damage was observed, and an outbuildings was destroyed.
column17: The first of twin tornadoes was reported by storm chasers.
column18: The second of twin tornadoes was reported by storm chasers.
column19: Trained storm spotters reported a brief tornado.
column20: An ethanol plant and a home sustained EF2 damage, while a feedlot and several other houses were impacted less severely. Trees, power poles, and grain bins were damaged, pivots were overturned, and a house had its roof partially blown off.
column21: A few train cars and irrigation pivots were overturned.
column22: A tornado was confirmed using video and radar information.
column23: Two outbuildings lost their roofs or were destroyed.
column24: A storm chaser observed a brief tornado.
column25: A trained storm spotter reported a brief tornado.
column26: Damage to trees and fencing was observed.
column27: Numerous trees, fences, and power poles were damaged. Several homes had their roofs damaged. HVAC equipment was damaged and light poles were downed at a hospital.
column28: A storm chaser observed a brief tornado.
column29: Storm chasers observed a potentially significant tornado that occurred in a rural area.
column30: A storm chaser observed a brief tornado.
column31: A home was leveled after a catastrophic failure of its garage door caused the structure to be lifted off its foundation and deposited {{convert|50|–|150|yd|m|abbr=on}} northeast. Two cars in the garage were only slightly moved. Nearby trees were snapped and debarked.
column33: An off-duty NWS employee observed a brief tornado.
column34: Photos of grain bin damage confirmed a tornado.
column35: Two homes sustained minor damage and trees were uprooted. Some damage was reported at the Tiger Safari Zoological park.
column37: Photos of damage to outbuildings confirmed a tornado.
column38: An emergency manager reported a brief tornado.
column39: A motel lost most of its second floor walls; many recreational vehicles at an adjacent RV park sustained significant damage.
column41: A storm chaser observed a brief tornado over open country.
column44: Storm chasers observed a large tornado moving across an open field.
column46: Storm chasers reported a tornado over rural areas.
column47: A trained storm spotter reported a brief tornado.
column48: Outbuildings, trees, and sheds sustained minor damage. The roofs of homes on farmsteads were damaged, and high-tension power lines were downed.
column49: The public observed a tornado crossing a field.
